security_privacy_cost_impact: data classification synthetic-only; secrets required false; network policy deny-unless-declared. No provider call, credential, migration or customer-data effect. Cost impact none: no metered resource is touched.
migration_and_data_impact: No migration is added or altered. db/foundation/prerequisites.sql is new and is deliberately NOT a migration: it sits outside db/foundation/migrations/, carries no batch number, joins no digest and reserves nothing in the registry. `make db-migrate-clean` applies it before batch 000, which is what makes the declared command self-sufficient on a database nobody prepared.
compatibility_impact: None to any contract. The changes are to DB-00's own lint, driver, assertion helpers and command wrapper, plus three files of A1's isolation suite that gain a `deniedOn` declaration on four cases -- no case's identity, statement, outcome or expectation moves. Two rules NARROW: an exemption register row no longer suppresses `rls_enabled`, and a row narrower than the catalog can corroborate no longer suppresses anything. The register is empty, so no committed catalog state changes meaning.
known_limitations: The live half runs in CI and nowhere else. A Postgres service container gives db-migrate-clean, db-schema-lint and db-rls-smoke a real database on every pull request; all SIX migration batches apply -- 000, 001, 002, 003, 004 and 010, counted from the tree rather than carried forward -- and the schema lint passes. The count read "five" from the moment batch 004 was added two commits later in the same night, on the same package, in a commit whose own blocker text says "Batch 004 exists"; C0's review D10 found it. This DEVELOPMENT HOST still has no psql, pg_ctl or docker, so the targets refuse locally and every live change is proven by a CI round, not from a shell. db-migrate-upgrade and db-seed-replay remain unproven for a different reason: neither has a fixture to run against, and both say so rather than reporting a pass.

What A0 can state, because it is a property of that document rather than a judgement about it: A1 re-measured the provisioned instance itself through ten read-only catalog queries rather than accepting A0's record, three of its findings contradict a record A0 wrote, and it declares in its own §0 that it is a subagent run in A0's vendor and model family assessing files it authored. The reservations that record raises are carried as the five blockers below, and they are open.

RESERVATION 1 (A1 §5.1) — REPAIRED, and the repair was then narrowed by C0's review D2. db/foundation/lint/rls-exemption-register.json exists and the schema lint reads it in BOTH directions, which is RFC-2026-016 §4's own wording and the difference between a control and a list: a table that is not forced with no row is refused, and a row whose exemption the catalog does not show is refused too -- because a register carrying exemptions nobody took cannot be read as complete, and completeness is the whole of what it proves about the tables that are NOT in it. Rows are held to the six fields the RFC names, to a known operation, and to a review date not older than the snapshot: an exemption does not age into permanence.

The register is EMPTY, and empty means something only because a non-empty one is checked. Six cases construct the situations rather than asserting on the file.

RESERVATION 2 (A1 §5.2) — REPAIRED, and the repair is what is now asserted. scripts/db/run.mjs asserts no service role is SUPERUSER as well as no service role holds BYPASSRLS, refuses a snapshot whose service_roles carry no superuser field at all (an unmeasured property must not read as a passing one), and pins the instance's superuser set the way it already pinned the bypass set. Measured 2026-09-06 on xtvtflkntpqfvflvdbwk: all three service roles rolsuper false; supabase_admin is the only rolsuper on the instance.

RESERVATION 3 (A1 §5.3/§5.4) — REPAIRED, and the correction is now a check rather than a comment. Batch 004 exists: it records both of batch 000's wrong claims (pgcrypto is not required for gen_random_uuid, which has been in pg_catalog since PG13; and `with schema public` was a no-op on the instance, where pgcrypto already lived in `extensions`), and it FAILS if gen_random_uuid is not resolvable unqualified or if pgcrypto is installed in public. That second assertion is what stops the CI/platform divergence returning: remove the shim line and this batch fails with the reason. Applied to the instance 2026-09-06 and the catalog snapshot retaken against migration set 7215963802260771.

000_foundation.sql's own text is unchanged: migration invariant 1 forbids rewriting an applied batch, which is why 003 corrected 002 the same way. The RFC status line inside its comment is still stale and is a decision-record status question, not a migration's.

What this repair COST, which was recorded nowhere until C0's review D3 measured it: because 000 and 004 are both applied and neither may be rewritten, the migration set became applicable only to a database where pgcrypto already exists outside `public`, and the only thing arranging that outside the platform was one line in a GitHub workflow. See the D3 entry below: the prerequisite is now part of `make db-migrate-clean` itself.

RESERVATION 4 (A1 §5.5) — REPAIRED at the call sites AND at the cause. The fixture and the invitation case now take the digest with pg_catalog's sha256(convert_to(...)), which resolves with no extension and no schema qualification; measured 2026-09-06 that it produces byte-identical output to extensions.digest(...,'sha256'), so no fixture identity moved. The cause was that the CI shim was MORE PERMISSIVE than the platform: batch 000's `create extension ... with schema public` is a no-op on the instance and succeeded in the container, so public.digest existed only in CI. The shim now installs pgcrypto in `extensions` where the platform has it, and the test that used to pin `public.digest(` now refuses any schema-qualified pgcrypto call.

Two consequences of that shim change were found later by C0. The pgcrypto placement has since moved out of the shim into db/foundation/prerequisites.sql, which db-migrate-clean applies itself (D3). And the reason attached to the test became false in both halves the moment the shim changed, because extensions.digest exists in the container now (D12). Both entries are below.

RESERVATION 5 (A1 §5.6) — REPAIRED, and the repair was then completed by C0's review D6. expectDeniedBy holds a case to the layer it declares, and the runner applies it to every case carrying deniedBy. A policy refusal always names the policy; anything else saying permission denied is the privilege layer; anything that classifies as neither fails rather than guessing. Silence stays silence: a case declaring no layer is not checked.

What that missed: a layer is not an attribution on its own. `permission denied for schema private` is 42501 and classifies as the same 'grant' layer as a refusal on the table under test, so the assertion said WHICH LAYER refused and never WHICH OBJECT. See the D6 entry below; a case now declares deniedOn beside deniedBy and the refusal must name that relation.

Tenant isolation is proven against the CI container and measured once against a provisioned Supabase instance, and the two prove different things. In CI, 28 isolation cases pass on every run and a NEGATIVE CONTROL disables row level security on app.workspaces and requires the suite to fail -- it reports 10 of 28, so the suite is not blind. What CI cannot establish is the platform: its roles come from db/foundation/ci/supabase-shim.sql and were created by us, so a green run means the policies still do what they did, never that this holds on Supabase. The BYPASSRLS measurement behind DATA-DEC-03 came from the provisioned instance and has no CI equivalent. Batches 020 and above own the assertions SMOKE_COVERAGE names as uncovered.

C0 CONTRACT REVIEW, 2026-09-06. The independent Reviewer run /claude/c0_contract_reviewer read the night's merged work and confirmed twelve defects. Its report is landed byte-for-byte at evidence/WP-0A-DB-00/c0-review-2026-09-06-night.md and is another run's record: it is not edited here, and the entries below dispose of it rather than restating it.

READ ITS §0 FIRST. C0 declares in its own words that it is a subagent spawned by A0 -- the author of everything it reviewed -- running in the same vendor and model family, on threads A0 chose. It therefore does NOT satisfy independence.prefer_cross_vendor_review, does not lift the cross_vendor_exception this package already carries, and must not be counted as the independent review this package owes. What it is: a second reading whose measurements against the tree stand on their own, every one of them re-runnable from the command or file:line it cites.

Disposition of the twelve: eight repaired here (D2, D3, D6, D7, D8, D9, D10, D12), one recorded without editing its source (D11), one carried open (D4), two belonging to other packages (D1 to WP-0A-CON-002, D5 to WP-0A-CON-008) and left alone. Each is an entry below.

D2 (MEDIUM-HIGH) — REPAIRED. WAS: the exemption register declared a granularity of role x table x operation and the lint enforced none of it. Rows were matched to a table by NAME alone, so a row scoped as narrowly as the shape allows -- {role: 'app_worker', operation: 'select'} -- bought its table a blanket pass, and the same row suppressed rls_enabled as well as rls_forced, which let one register row excuse a tenant table having no row level security at all.

IS NOW: the lint enforces what the catalog can CORROBORATE, and scripts/db/run.mjs and the register's own _what_the_catalog_can_corroborate say plainly what that is. relforcerowsecurity is a TABLE property -- one value for every role and every operation at once -- so it corroborates exactly one row, role '*' with operation 'all', and only such a row suppresses the unforced-table finding. rolbypassrls and rolsuper are ROLE properties holding for every table at once, so a row naming a role is checked against that role's own attributes and suppresses no table finding; naming a table in it narrows nothing. NOTHING in the snapshot is per-operation -- it counts a table's policies and never records which command one is for -- so an operation other than 'all' is refused as uncorroborable in either direction, which is the same unfalsifiable shape §4 retired 'force where compatible' for being. rls_enabled is not exemptible at all: RFC-2026-012 commits the whole client/database boundary to row level security and §4 retired only the FORCE condition.

Three new cases in test-kits/db/foundation-contract.test.mjs, and the ACCEPTED row in one of them is {role: 'service_role', operation: 'all'} -- corroborated by the catalog's measured roles_bypassing_rls -- so the accept direction is no longer always the maximal exemption.

D3 (MEDIUM) — REPAIRED. WAS: `make db-migrate-clean` was no longer self-sufficient. Batch 004 raises if pgcrypto is in `public` and batch 000 puts it there on any database nobody prepared; both are applied and migration invariant 1 forbids rewriting either, so the set was applicable only where pgcrypto already existed outside `public`. That held on the provisioned instance by the platform's doing and in CI by ONE LINE INSIDE A GITHUB WORKFLOW -- `psql -f db/foundation/ci/supabase-shim.sql` before the make target. The repository's own declared command could not apply its own migration set to a bare Postgres, and nothing recorded the cost.

IS NOW: the prerequisite is part of the declared command. db/foundation/prerequisites.sql holds the two statements the migration set actually requires -- `create schema if not exists extensions` and `create extension if not exists pgcrypto with schema extensions` -- and scripts/db/run.mjs applies it as the first step of migrate-clean, exposed as migrateCleanSteps() so a test asserts on the steps the target runs rather than on this file's text. It is deliberately NOT a migration: it sits outside db/foundation/migrations/, carries no batch number, joins no digest and reserves nothing, so the catalog snapshot's taken_against_migrations does not go stale (asserted).

The shim LOST those two lines and keeps everything that is genuinely Supabase emulation -- the auth schema, auth.uid(), the three platform roles -- and keeps its header saying what it is not. That is the part that makes the repair observable: CI no longer satisfies the prerequisite in advance, so the container reaching batch 000 with pgcrypto in `extensions` is now the command's doing, and if migrate-clean stops applying it, batch 004 fails the build. A test pins that the shim does not create pgcrypto.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN: this host has no psql and no docker, so the bare-Postgres path is argued from the SQL and pinned by the step list, not executed. The first CI round on this branch is what executes it.

D6 (MEDIUM-LOW) — REPAIRED. WAS: expectDeniedBy attributed a LAYER without attributing an OBJECT. `permission denied` is a catch-all, so `permission denied for schema private` -- the exact failure this harness produced on all seven no-effect cases -- classified as the same 'grant' layer as `permission denied for table workspace_invitations`. A case declaring deniedBy: 'grant' therefore passed when the refusal came from a privilege problem in the SCAFFOLDING rather than on the object under test.

IS NOW: db/foundation/test-helpers/rls-assertions.mjs carries denialObject() beside denialLayer(), reading which relation, schema or function the message names, and expectDeniedBy takes the case's declared object. A refusal naming a schema or a function, or naming a different table, or naming nothing at all, fails the case rather than satisfying it. The four cases carrying deniedBy now declare deniedOn (workspace_invitations, workspace_invitations, workspaces, workspace_members), run-isolation.mjs passes it, and identity-isolation.test.mjs pins statically that the two are declared together and that the declared object appears in the case's own statement -- so a future case cannot name a layer and no object. Silence is still not a claim: a case declaring neither is checked for neither.

C0's other observation on this finding stands unrepaired and is not a defect: no live case declares deniedBy: 'policy', so in the live suite the discriminator only ever runs its catch-all arm. The policy branch is exercised by the unit test. Writing a live policy-layer case is batch 020's, which owns the first table with a client-writable column the matrix marks S.

D7 (LOW, privilege path) — REPAIRED. WAS: `reset role;` was injected into a case's prelude by matching /\bprivate\.as_/ against the SQL AFTER parameter values had been inlined into it. A case whose parameter carried that literal text -- and the cases do pass free-text names like 'renamed by the service' -- would have had its own statement run as the administrative connection role instead of the identity under test. No fixture value triggered it and the escalation was confined to a rolled-back transaction; the shape was the defect.

IS NOW: the decision is taken from the STATEMENT before substitution, in scripts/db/rls-smoke.mjs, and the escaping of values is unchanged. bufferedDriver takes its query function as a seam so the SQL it assembles is observable, and a test drives it with a parameter containing `private.as_service`, asserts no reset is emitted, asserts the value still reaches the statement, and asserts a real identity call still gets its reset.

D8 (LOW, latent) — REPAIRED. WAS: the result boundary could be moved by data, and moved forward silently. One marker was selected before the statement and everything after its LAST occurrence was parsed, so a marker appearing in the statement's own output won the search: the region became a suffix of the real result whose first line was then eaten as a header, and a single occurrence in the final row yielded ZERO ROWS -- a PASS for expectNoRows and for half one of expectNoEffect. Separately, the EPILOGUE was inside the parsed region, so anything it printed became extra rows of the statement's result; that was safe only because the sole caller passes `rollback;`, and nothing in the signature or a test said an epilogue had to be silent.

IS NOW: the result is FENCED between two markers, and scripts/db/psql-driver.mjs counts them instead of searching. Each marker select prints its marker exactly twice -- column name, then value -- so 2 and 2 is the only shape the driver emits; any other count means output somewhere carried a marker and resultRegion() returns an error rather than choosing an occurrence. The epilogue is now structurally outside the region whatever it prints. Two cases pin it: a workspace whose NAME carries the marker produces no region at all, and a chatty epilogue does not become rows of the statement it follows.

Still true, still by convention: a statement containing two statements has both outputs folded into one region, and a statement returning no result set parses to [] indistinguishably from a header with no rows. identity-isolation.test.mjs asserts statically that every mutation case carries RETURNING, which is what makes the second safe. Both are recorded in the driver's own comment.

D9 (LOW) — REPAIRED, as a corrected claim rather than as a changed mechanism. WAS: rls-assertions.mjs argued that matching on message text is legitimate because "LC_ALL=C is set by the driver and by CI, so the English text is the text". The premise is true and the inference is not: `permission denied for table ...` and `new row violates row-level security policy for table ...` are SERVER-generated, so their language is the server's lc_messages GUC, which the client's environment does not reach and which is SUSET, so the driver cannot set it through PGOPTIONS either. LC_ALL=C governs libpq's own client-side text, a different set of messages.

IS NOW: the comment says that, and says why it was a wrong guarantee rather than an unsafe one -- against a server with a localised lc_messages, denialLayer returns null and expectDeniedBy THROWS naming the message it could not attribute, while expectDenied is unaffected because SQLSTATE is locale-independent. A new case drives a localised refusal through both and pins that the refusal still classifies, the layer does not, and a case declaring EITHER layer fails rather than passing on the catch-all arm. In CI the postgres:17 image initdbs under en_US.utf8, which is why the English text arrives there.

D10 (LOW) — REPAIRED. WAS: open_blockers[0] and the same sentence in handoffs/WP-0A-DB-00-author-handoff.json said "all five migration batches apply". There are six: 000, 001, 002, 003, 004, 010. The count was correct when the blocker was rewritten and stopped being correct two commits later, in the same night, on the same package, in a commit whose own blocker text says "Batch 004 exists". IS NOW: six in both places, counted from the tree, with the reason it went stale recorded beside it.

D11 (LOW) — RECORDED HERE, NOT REPAIRED AT ITS SOURCE. evidence/WP-0A-DB-00/a1-countersignature-role-topology.md:128 reads "10 of 28, as `open_blockers[2]` states". When A1 wrote it the tenant-isolation blocker WAS at index 2; PR #64 inserted five RESERVATION entries at indices 2 to 6 and moved it to INDEX 7, where it still is (verified against this file). open_blockers[2] now reads "RESERVATION 1 (A1 §5.1)...", a different subject entirely.

A1's countersignature is another run's record and A0 does not edit it, which is also C0's own recommendation. The correction lives here instead: the blocker A1 cites is open_blockers[7], not [2], and the 10-of-28 figure it supports is unaffected -- C0 re-derived it independently and it matches A1's list case for case. The finding's real lesson is the one this repository has spent the night acting on: a positional citation into a mutable array rots, and it has now done so in the evidence layer as well as in the blockers.

D12 (LOW) — REPAIRED. WAS: tests/db/identity/identity-isolation.test.mjs asserted, correctly, that the fixture takes its digest through no schema-qualified pgcrypto call -- and justified it with a sentence false in both halves: "`public.digest` does not exist on the provisioned instance and `extensions.digest` does not exist in the CI container". The CI shim, added in the same increment, installs pgcrypto in `extensions`, so extensions.digest DOES exist in the container and public.digest exists in neither place. IS NOW: the assertion is unchanged and its reason says the true thing -- where pgcrypto lives is an environment fact (`extensions` on the instance and in CI, `public` on a database nobody prepared), so a fixture that names a schema is a fixture that runs in one of them, and pg_catalog's sha256() resolves in all of them.

D4 (MEDIUM) — CARRIED OPEN, NOT REPAIRED, and the reason is that this run cannot reproduce it. C0 found that the auth-context guard's stated property -- outside a transaction block SET LOCAL is a no-op, so the read-back returns the previous value and the helper raises -- is asserted by a regex over the helper's own SOURCE TEXT and by nothing that executes it. That is a real observation about the test, and it is the third proxy in a row on this guard.

What cannot be decided here is whether the property itself holds: does set_config(name, value, true) inside an implicit single-statement transaction apply the value, making the read-back always succeed and the guard inert, or is it skipped, making the guard work? C0 could not settle it and listed it in its own §5 as unverified; this host has no psql and no docker either. Writing a behavioural test against a property nobody has measured would produce a test that passes for a reason nobody knows, which is the defect class this package exists to remove, and replacing the guard on a guess would be the fourth proxy. It needs one query against a live server -- `select private.as_anonymous();` outside begin/commit -- and the run that has one owns the repair. Until then the source-text assertion stands and is described here as what it is.

D1 and D5 are NOT this package's and were not touched. D1 (HIGH) is a blocker in work-packages/WP-0A-CON-002.json and its handoff that declares RFC-2026-002's manual merge control retired from inside a work-package manifest; it belongs to WP-0A-CON-002 and is being repaired there. D5 (MEDIUM) is scripts/refresh-author-handoff.mjs blanking a handoff on a branch already merged to main; it belongs to WP-0A-CON-008. Editing another package's manifest or another package's script from this branch is the ownership defect this repository's branch-scope guard exists to catch, and agreeing with a finding is not authority over the file it lands in.

What that missed: a layer is not an attribution on its own. `permission denied for schema private` is 42501 and classifies as the same 'grant' layer as a refusal on the table under test, so the assertion said WHICH LAYER refused and never WHICH OBJECT. See the D6 entry below; a case now declares deniedOn beside deniedBy and the refusal must name that relation.

Tenant isolation is proven against the CI container and measured once against a provisioned Supabase instance, and the two prove different things. In CI, 28 isolation cases pass on every run and a NEGATIVE CONTROL disables row level security on app.workspaces and requires the suite to fail -- it reports 10 of 28, so the suite is not blind. What CI cannot establish is the platform: its roles come from db/foundation/ci/supabase-shim.sql and were created by us, so a green run means the policies still do what they did, never that this holds on Supabase. The BYPASSRLS measurement behind DATA-DEC-03 came from the provisioned instance and has no CI equivalent. Batches 020 and above own the assertions SMOKE_COVERAGE names as uncovered.

C0 CONTRACT REVIEW, 2026-09-06. The independent Reviewer run /claude/c0_contract_reviewer read the night's merged work and confirmed twelve defects. Its report is landed byte-for-byte at evidence/WP-0A-DB-00/c0-review-2026-09-06-night.md and is another run's record: it is not edited here, and the entries below dispose of it rather than restating it.

READ ITS §0 FIRST. C0 declares in its own words that it is a subagent spawned by A0 -- the author of everything it reviewed -- running in the same vendor and model family, on threads A0 chose. It therefore does NOT satisfy independence.prefer_cross_vendor_review, does not lift the cross_vendor_exception this package already carries, and must not be counted as the independent review this package owes. What it is: a second reading whose measurements against the tree stand on their own, every one of them re-runnable from the command or file:line it cites.

Disposition of the twelve: eight repaired here (D2, D3, D6, D7, D8, D9, D10, D12), one recorded without editing its source (D11), one carried open (D4), two belonging to other packages (D1 to WP-0A-CON-002, D5 to WP-0A-CON-008) and left alone. Each is an entry below.

D2 (MEDIUM-HIGH) — REPAIRED. WAS: the exemption register declared a granularity of role x table x operation and the lint enforced none of it. Rows were matched to a table by NAME alone, so a row scoped as narrowly as the shape allows -- {role: 'app_worker', operation: 'select'} -- bought its table a blanket pass, and the same row suppressed rls_enabled as well as rls_forced, which let one register row excuse a tenant table having no row level security at all.

IS NOW: the lint enforces what the catalog can CORROBORATE, and scripts/db/run.mjs and the register's own _what_the_catalog_can_corroborate say plainly what that is. relforcerowsecurity is a TABLE property -- one value for every role and every operation at once -- so it corroborates exactly one row, role '*' with operation 'all', and only such a row suppresses the unforced-table finding. rolbypassrls and rolsuper are ROLE properties holding for every table at once, so a row naming a role is checked against that role's own attributes and suppresses no table finding; naming a table in it narrows nothing. NOTHING in the snapshot is per-operation -- it counts a table's policies and never records which command one is for -- so an operation other than 'all' is refused as uncorroborable in either direction, which is the same unfalsifiable shape §4 retired 'force where compatible' for being. rls_enabled is not exemptible at all: RFC-2026-012 commits the whole client/database boundary to row level security and §4 retired only the FORCE condition.

Three new cases in test-kits/db/foundation-contract.test.mjs, and the ACCEPTED row in one of them is {role: 'service_role', operation: 'all'} -- corroborated by the catalog's measured roles_bypassing_rls -- so the accept direction is no longer always the maximal exemption.

D3 (MEDIUM) — REPAIRED. WAS: `make db-migrate-clean` was no longer self-sufficient. Batch 004 raises if pgcrypto is in `public` and batch 000 puts it there on any database nobody prepared; both are applied and migration invariant 1 forbids rewriting either, so the set was applicable only where pgcrypto already existed outside `public`. That held on the provisioned instance by the platform's doing and in CI by ONE LINE INSIDE A GITHUB WORKFLOW -- `psql -f db/foundation/ci/supabase-shim.sql` before the make target. The repository's own declared command could not apply its own migration set to a bare Postgres, and nothing recorded the cost.

IS NOW: the prerequisite is part of the declared command. db/foundation/prerequisites.sql holds the two statements the migration set actually requires -- `create schema if not exists extensions` and `create extension if not exists pgcrypto with schema extensions` -- and scripts/db/run.mjs applies it as the first step of migrate-clean, exposed as migrateCleanSteps() so a test asserts on the steps the target runs rather than on this file's text. It is deliberately NOT a migration: it sits outside db/foundation/migrations/, carries no batch number, joins no digest and reserves nothing, so the catalog snapshot's taken_against_migrations does not go stale (asserted).

The shim LOST those two lines and keeps everything that is genuinely Supabase emulation -- the auth schema, auth.uid(), the three platform roles -- and keeps its header saying what it is not. That is the part that makes the repair observable: CI no longer satisfies the prerequisite in advance, so the container reaching batch 000 with pgcrypto in `extensions` is now the command's doing, and if migrate-clean stops applying it, batch 004 fails the build. A test pins that the shim does not create pgcrypto.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN: this host has no psql and no docker, so the bare-Postgres path is argued from the SQL and pinned by the step list, not executed. The first CI round on this branch is what executes it.

D6 (MEDIUM-LOW) — REPAIRED. WAS: expectDeniedBy attributed a LAYER without attributing an OBJECT. `permission denied` is a catch-all, so `permission denied for schema private` -- the exact failure this harness produced on all seven no-effect cases -- classified as the same 'grant' layer as `permission denied for table workspace_invitations`. A case declaring deniedBy: 'grant' therefore passed when the refusal came from a privilege problem in the SCAFFOLDING rather than on the object under test.

IS NOW: db/foundation/test-helpers/rls-assertions.mjs carries denialObject() beside denialLayer(), reading which relation, schema or function the message names, and expectDeniedBy takes the case's declared object. A refusal naming a schema or a function, or naming a different table, or naming nothing at all, fails the case rather than satisfying it. The four cases carrying deniedBy now declare deniedOn (workspace_invitations, workspace_invitations, workspaces, workspace_members), run-isolation.mjs passes it, and identity-isolation.test.mjs pins statically that the two are declared together and that the declared object appears in the case's own statement -- so a future case cannot name a layer and no object. Silence is still not a claim: a case declaring neither is checked for neither.

C0's other observation on this finding stands unrepaired and is not a defect: no live case declares deniedBy: 'policy', so in the live suite the discriminator only ever runs its catch-all arm. The policy branch is exercised by the unit test. Writing a live policy-layer case is batch 020's, which owns the first table with a client-writable column the matrix marks S.

D7 (LOW, privilege path) — REPAIRED. WAS: `reset role;` was injected into a case's prelude by matching /\bprivate\.as_/ against the SQL AFTER parameter values had been inlined into it. A case whose parameter carried that literal text -- and the cases do pass free-text names like 'renamed by the service' -- would have had its own statement run as the administrative connection role instead of the identity under test. No fixture value triggered it and the escalation was confined to a rolled-back transaction; the shape was the defect.

IS NOW: the decision is taken from the STATEMENT before substitution, in scripts/db/rls-smoke.mjs, and the escaping of values is unchanged. bufferedDriver takes its query function as a seam so the SQL it assembles is observable, and a test drives it with a parameter containing `private.as_service`, asserts no reset is emitted, asserts the value still reaches the statement, and asserts a real identity call still gets its reset.

D8 (LOW, latent) — REPAIRED. WAS: the result boundary could be moved by data, and moved forward silently. One marker was selected before the statement and everything after its LAST occurrence was parsed, so a marker appearing in the statement's own output won the search: the region became a suffix of the real result whose first line was then eaten as a header, and a single occurrence in the final row yielded ZERO ROWS -- a PASS for expectNoRows and for half one of expectNoEffect. Separately, the EPILOGUE was inside the parsed region, so anything it printed became extra rows of the statement's result; that was safe only because the sole caller passes `rollback;`, and nothing in the signature or a test said an epilogue had to be silent.

IS NOW: the result is FENCED between two markers, and scripts/db/psql-driver.mjs counts them instead of searching. Each marker select prints its marker exactly twice -- column name, then value -- so 2 and 2 is the only shape the driver emits; any other count means output somewhere carried a marker and resultRegion() returns an error rather than choosing an occurrence. The epilogue is now structurally outside the region whatever it prints. Two cases pin it: a workspace whose NAME carries the marker produces no region at all, and a chatty epilogue does not become rows of the statement it follows.

Still true, still by convention: a statement containing two statements has both outputs folded into one region, and a statement returning no result set parses to [] indistinguishably from a header with no rows. identity-isolation.test.mjs asserts statically that every mutation case carries RETURNING, which is what makes the second safe. Both are recorded in the driver's own comment.

D9 (LOW) — REPAIRED, as a corrected claim rather than as a changed mechanism. WAS: rls-assertions.mjs argued that matching on message text is legitimate because "LC_ALL=C is set by the driver and by CI, so the English text is the text". The premise is true and the inference is not: `permission denied for table ...` and `new row violates row-level security policy for table ...` are SERVER-generated, so their language is the server's lc_messages GUC, which the client's environment does not reach and which is SUSET, so the driver cannot set it through PGOPTIONS either. LC_ALL=C governs libpq's own client-side text, a different set of messages.

IS NOW: the comment says that, and says why it was a wrong guarantee rather than an unsafe one -- against a server with a localised lc_messages, denialLayer returns null and expectDeniedBy THROWS naming the message it could not attribute, while expectDenied is unaffected because SQLSTATE is locale-independent. A new case drives a localised refusal through both and pins that the refusal still classifies, the layer does not, and a case declaring EITHER layer fails rather than passing on the catch-all arm. In CI the postgres:17 image initdbs under en_US.utf8, which is why the English text arrives there.

D10 (LOW) — REPAIRED. WAS: open_blockers[0] and the same sentence in handoffs/WP-0A-DB-00-author-handoff.json said "all five migration batches apply". There are six: 000, 001, 002, 003, 004, 010. The count was correct when the blocker was rewritten and stopped being correct two commits later, in the same night, on the same package, in a commit whose own blocker text says "Batch 004 exists". IS NOW: six in both places, counted from the tree, with the reason it went stale recorded beside it.

D11 (LOW) — RECORDED HERE, NOT REPAIRED AT ITS SOURCE. evidence/WP-0A-DB-00/a1-countersignature-role-topology.md:128 reads "10 of 28, as `open_blockers[2]` states". When A1 wrote it the tenant-isolation blocker WAS at index 2; PR #64 inserted five RESERVATION entries at indices 2 to 6 and moved it to INDEX 7, where it still is (verified against this file). open_blockers[2] now reads "RESERVATION 1 (A1 §5.1)...", a different subject entirely.

A1's countersignature is another run's record and A0 does not edit it, which is also C0's own recommendation. The correction lives here instead: the blocker A1 cites is open_blockers[7], not [2], and the 10-of-28 figure it supports is unaffected -- C0 re-derived it independently and it matches A1's list case for case. The finding's real lesson is the one this repository has spent the night acting on: a positional citation into a mutable array rots, and it has now done so in the evidence layer as well as in the blockers.

D12 (LOW) — REPAIRED. WAS: tests/db/identity/identity-isolation.test.mjs asserted, correctly, that the fixture takes its digest through no schema-qualified pgcrypto call -- and justified it with a sentence false in both halves: "`public.digest` does not exist on the provisioned instance and `extensions.digest` does not exist in the CI container". The CI shim, added in the same increment, installs pgcrypto in `extensions`, so extensions.digest DOES exist in the container and public.digest exists in neither place. IS NOW: the assertion is unchanged and its reason says the true thing -- where pgcrypto lives is an environment fact (`extensions` on the instance and in CI, `public` on a database nobody prepared), so a fixture that names a schema is a fixture that runs in one of them, and pg_catalog's sha256() resolves in all of them.

D4 (MEDIUM) — CARRIED OPEN, NOT REPAIRED, and the reason is that this run cannot reproduce it. C0 found that the auth-context guard's stated property -- outside a transaction block SET LOCAL is a no-op, so the read-back returns the previous value and the helper raises -- is asserted by a regex over the helper's own SOURCE TEXT and by nothing that executes it. That is a real observation about the test, and it is the third proxy in a row on this guard.

What cannot be decided here is whether the property itself holds: does set_config(name, value, true) inside an implicit single-statement transaction apply the value, making the read-back always succeed and the guard inert, or is it skipped, making the guard work? C0 could not settle it and listed it in its own §5 as unverified; this host has no psql and no docker either. Writing a behavioural test against a property nobody has measured would produce a test that passes for a reason nobody knows, which is the defect class this package exists to remove, and replacing the guard on a guess would be the fourth proxy. It needs one query against a live server -- `select private.as_anonymous();` outside begin/commit -- and the run that has one owns the repair. Until then the source-text assertion stands and is described here as what it is.

D1 and D5 are NOT this package's and were not touched. D1 (HIGH) is a blocker in work-packages/WP-0A-CON-002.json and its handoff that declares RFC-2026-002's manual merge control retired from inside a work-package manifest; it belongs to WP-0A-CON-002 and is being repaired there.
